title: Tethys Systems – SI/Channel + Cloud GPU Fit Discovery (Notes v2)
summary: Updated internal notes from Redwood ↔ Tethys Systems discovery on a channel + SI partnership. Tethys wants to resell and operate Redwood inference for enterprise customers, with a focus on (1) real-time chat latency and (2) high-throughput embedding/batch. We discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment modes, security/compliance requirements (SSO/SAML, audit logs, customer-managed keys), commercial structure (reseller discount + Dedicated commits), and a pilot plan. This v2 incorporates post-call clarifications from SE + Partnerships and updates the pilot timeline/owners.
key_updates_since_v1:
- Pilot timing adjusted: target 6-week pilot remains, but exec alignment moved due to calendar conflicts.
- Security clarification: Customer-managed KMS supported for Private (VPC + on-prem). HSM-backed key wrapping is supported for on-prem Private today; for VPC Private it is supported in limited clouds/regions and requires a scoping call with Security Eng.
- EU Private (VPC) lead time updated: plan for 3–5 weeks (was previously stated as 2–4) depending on peering/private link approvals and key management setup.
- Commercial clarification: reseller discount applies to usage; Dedicated commitments can be booked either (a) end-customer direct with referral/crediting, or (b) partner-led with pass-through commit—legal prefers (a) unless Tethys is acting as reseller-of-record.
- Perf baseline deliverable changed: first pass will be a modeled estimate using trace stats, followed by a hosted benchmark once sample data is approved for transfer.
topics: technical integration patterns (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem)

deployment_modes_notes:
Hosted API: fastest start; easiest for pilot; isolation is logical but not customer-controlled network.
Dedicated: reserved capacity; better predictability for latency/throughput; can support autoscaling within reserved pool; discussed burst behavior and fallbacks to alternate variants when constrained.
Private: VPC or on-prem; required for a subset of Tethys regulated customers. Needs network topology sign-off (peering/private link), audit logging, and customer-managed keys. Expect longer provisioning + approvals.
technical_notes:
Integration:
- REST API + SDKs available.
- Private deployments: delivered via deploy pack (Helm + manifests); operator-based install supported for on-prem and some managed K8s environments.

Networking (Private/VPC):
- Supports direct VPC peering and private-link equivalents depending on cloud/region.
- Need to document traffic flow, egress paths, and customer responsibility boundaries.

Performance:
- Tethys stated initial target: ~50 QPS for chat + weekly batch embeddings (~2M).
- Jonas to start with a modeled estimate (needs QPS distribution, seq length, token mix) and then run hosted baseline benchmark after data-transfer approval.

Caching/KV:
- Runtime supports continuous batching; KV cache behavior depends on seq length distribution.
- Option for session pinning/stickiness for certain flows to keep KV warm (validate suitability for their multi-tenant managed offering).

Model catalog:
- Curated catalog; partner-requested models possible with licensing + compatibility validation.
- Quantization profiles: recommended A/B testing required for high-fidelity workloads (legal text use case mentioned).
security_compliance_notes:
Tethys requirements mentioned: finance/healthcare customers, EU residency, auditability.
- SSO/SAML: supported.
- Audit logs: supported; confirm log sink options for Private.
- Customer-managed keys: supported for Private. For VPC Private, key integration options vary by cloud and may require additional scoping.
- SOC 2 Type II + ISO summaries: available under NDA (redacted reports).
- Data residency: Hosted in EU region is possible, but contractual residency guarantees vary; Private EU is the stronger posture but has longer lead times.
commercial_notes:
Tethys interest: reseller + managed services; wants to own billing in some deals.
- We can support partner billing via reseller arrangements and some marketplace flows.
- White-label UI: generally not for Hosted; more feasible for Dedicated/Private where partner can front their own portal/billing and integrate Redwood runtime.
- Discounting: typical reseller discount on usage; Dedicated commit pricing/tiers handled via addendum; volume tiers to be shared via margin sheet.
- Co-sell: lead credits/co-sell enablement available for priority partners (include in partner packet).
- Request from Tethys: sample SLA/support tiers + example reseller term sheet template.
competitors_mentioned: ApexCompute; NimbusGrid (from call). Additional competitive note from Maya follow-up: Tethys also evaluating "generic GPU brokers" but did not name vendors.
pilot_proposal:
Goal: validate technical fit + economics for Tethys-managed enterprise workloads.
Suggested structure:
1) Week 0–1: hosted baseline + integration walkthrough (API/SDK, auth, logging).
2) Week 2–4: Dedicated profile estimate + optional reserved-capacity test (subject to sample workload readiness).
3) Week 4–6: 1–2 design partners identified by Tethys; measure latency SLOs, throughput, and cost per unit.
Success metrics (draft): p95 latency target agreed per workload; embedding unit cost target; integration effort within agreed engineering-week budget; security checklist signed off for at least one regulated customer profile.
Open point: if EU Private is mandatory for the first design partner, pilot schedule must accommodate 3–5 week provisioning window.
risks_open_questions:
- Data transfer: need clarity on what sample prompts/embeddings can be shared; if restricted, benchmarking must stay modeled until a secure transfer method is approved.
- Private EU lead time: could delay pilot start if first customer requires Private from day 1.
- Reseller-of-record vs referral: legal/compliance implications for partner owning billing; need to confirm preferred contracting path early.
- HSM support expectations: Tethys asked about HSM; we need to scope cloud/region specifics for VPC Private and avoid over-committing.
- Marketplace: helpful for Tethys GTM, but listing/timing depends on internal readiness and packaging.

body:
Context
- Source: Fireflies recording tethys-20250327-01 + internal follow-ups.
- Participants (from call): Maya Patel (AE), Jonas Reed (SE); Sofia Alvarez (Head of Partnerships), Ravi Menon (Lead Cloud Architect), Diane Cho (Biz Dev).

What Tethys wants
- Package Redwood into a managed SI offering (resell + operate).
- Serve two primary workload shapes: low-latency chat and high-throughput embeddings/batch.
- Support enterprise procurement patterns including partner-owned billing in some cases.

Redwood positioning (as presented)
- Hosted API: quickest start, easiest onboarding.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity + predictable performance; can add autoscaling policies within reserved footprint; discuss burst/fallback behaviors for spiky loads.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated customers; requires network + key management + audit logging alignment; longer lead time.

Key customer requirements captured
- Data residency (EU noted).
- SSO/SAML, audit logs, customer-managed keys (KMS).
- Clear network topology and egress story (peering/private link).
- Commercials: partner margin/discount, Dedicated commit structures, potential marketplace path.

Clarifications to avoid surprises
- HSM: supported strongly for on-prem Private; VPC Private support varies and must be scoped.
- EU Private: plan 3–5 weeks provisioning in many cases due to approvals and setup.
- Benchmarking: start modeled, then run hosted baseline once sample data transfer is approved.

Requests from Tethys
- Sample SLA + support tiers for Dedicated.
- Example reseller contract term sheet.
- Clear explanation of fallbacks/routing when regional capacity is constrained.

Internal note
- Keep language consistent: product is "Redwood Optimize" (not "Optimise").
- Ensure partner packet includes: GTM enablement, co-sell/lead credit rules, margin sheet, and a crisp decision tree for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
